objective: Bound and strictly parse the untrusted ROS 2 TaskEvent capture before any event is appended, so an oversized, duplicate-key or non-finite capture is refused as a whole with a typed error instead of being ingested or stored as a prefix of itself.
decision_supported: Whether a captured runtime TaskEvent log can be trusted as execution evidence without a capture size, line count, duplicate-key or non-finite value making the stored record ambiguous or unbounded.
acceptance: a capture whose bytes exceed MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES is refused before any line is decoded, and the refusal names the path and the byte limit
a capture with more than MAX_CAPTURE_LINES nonblank lines is refused before any line is parsed
a duplicate object key at any nesting level inside one capture line is refused rather than resolved to one of the duplicate values
the bare NaN, Infinity and -Infinity constants are refused, so no non-finite value can be bound into an action_result
a refused capture writes no event and leaves the store exactly as it was, because every line is decoded and bound before the first append
the refusal names the file path or the failing line and the exceeded limit, and never echoes the capture body
the existing exact-retry, restart-replay and correlation tests still pass unchanged
evidence: targeted pytest output for the oversize-byte, oversize-line, duplicate-key, non-finite and unchanged-store cases
the seeded property corpus now includes capture-file cases whose valid prefix would otherwise be stored, and its case count stays above the committed minimum
ruff check and ruff format --check output for the changed files
the Task Packet changed-path validation output against origin/main
stop_conditions: stop if bounding the capture would require a live ROS 2 or DDS dependency, because ROS 2 is not a Workbench dependency
stop if the fix would require editing interfaces/, libs/contracts/, services/ or a new WorldEventType
stop if a capture can only be kept under the limit by truncating it and ingesting a prefix, because a truncated capture is a silently partial evidence chain
stop if a modification outside allowed_paths is required
risks_and_fallbacks: A runtime capture could legitimately exceed the committed budget; fallback is that the capture is refused with the limit named rather than ingested partially, and the limits live in one place so a reviewed change can raise them

A duplicate-key refusal could reject a capture a lenient consumer would have accepted; fallback is that the refusal names the key, so the runtime side can fix the message rather than the evidence being silently ambiguous

Rejecting a capture before appending means a store-level failure part-way through a batch can still leave earlier lines written; fallback is that those lines carry the runtime's own event identity, so re-ingesting the same capture replays them instead of duplicating results
rollback is a revert of this commit; the change adds no dependency, touches no schema or store, and leaves the successful-ingest path unchanged
